Dhāmī Sect
------------------------------------------
Some of the mystics of medieval India made serious attempts to weld the Hindus and the Muslims into one great brother-hood. Prāṇanātha was one of them. He must have lived during the period A.

-1750. He was an adept in the scriptures of both हिन्दुइस्म् and Islam. He founded a sect called the ‘Dhāmī Sect,’ which was monotheistic in character and liberal in outlook.
Members of this sect call God as ‘dhāman or Home’. Their religious life is founded on moral purity, compassion, service and love of humanity. In their places of worship, both Hindus and Muslims pray together.

dhāma
(‘abode’)
------------------------------------------
The word means an abode or a sacred place, a place of पिल्ग्रिमगे.
The four well-known pilgrim centers—Badarīnātha in the north, जगन्नाथ-पुरी or पुरी in the east, Rāmeśvara in the South and द्वारका in the west—are specially known as ‘Caturdhāmas’ (Cār Dhām in Hindī) and are coveted places of पिल्ग्रिमगे for all the Hindus.
It is obvious that in the attempt at a visit to these centres, practically all the other important places of पिल्ग्रिमगे all over India too, are covered.
